invariants.text: Develop SMALL to BIG: implement one version at a time, and do not begin a later version until the user explicitly instructs it.
V1 contains only basic remember and recall behavior. JEV admission, contradiction handling, lifecycle, advanced retrieval, memory types, and multi-agent features are out of scope.
Prefer the standard library and add infrastructure or dependencies only when an observed limitation justifies them. Every version must include executable tests and document discovered limitations.

decisions.title: Use an in-memory V1 store behind a concrete interface
decisions.text: The adopted V1 uses a list-backed MemoryStore and a small MemoryInterface because this is enough to prove in-process remember and recall while preserving a future insertion seam for JEV. Persistence, databases, and abstract factories are deferred until evidence requires them.

decisions.title: Treat the V1 architecture as a proposal
decisions.text: The list-backed MemoryStore, concrete MemoryInterface, four-field Memory model, and substring retrieval remain proposed design choices. They must proceed through Genesis specification and planning approval before implementation.

knowledge.title: Adopted V1 baseline
knowledge.text: V1 consists of experiments/v1/memory.py, tests/test_memory.py, README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, and ROADMAP.md. It uses a standard-library in-memory store, a concrete MemoryInterface, and case-insensitive substring retrieval. The verification command is python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v and currently passes two tests.
knowledge.source: User project brief and adopted repository, 2026-09-26

knowledge.title: Pre-implementation discovery baseline
knowledge.text: The earlier V1 implementation and tests were removed at the user's request. The repository now contains Genesis state and planning documentation only; no memory behavior is implemented or verified.
